fields.title: Why quality drops as the corpus grows
fields.keyTakeaway: As the corpus grows, precision drops. Pre-search filtering usually yields more than improving the search itself — and the decision on filters is a product decision.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: It worked on a hundred documents, but got worse on ten thousand. What changed?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: This is the most frequent surprise in AI products: the demo works, but production does not. The cause is structural, and knowing it lets you bake the solution in immediately.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Three things change as the corpus grows.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **The number of similar documents grows.** On a hundred products, the query "lactose-free milk" finds the right one. On forty thousand, it finds a hundred similar ones, and the correct one might not make it to the top.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **[[precision|Precision]] drops while [[recall|recall]] stays the same.** To find the right item, you have to take more candidates, which dilutes the context.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Heterogeneity grows.** Documents vary in type, quality, and format. Uniform chunking stops working for all of them.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: *Pre-search filtering.* Narrow the scope: only this store, only this category. Sharply increases precision and is almost free. A product decision — which filters are available. *Hybrid search.* Vector search finds by meaning, text search by exact matches like SKU codes and brand names. Together they are noticeably better. *Reranking.* Take 50 candidates, select the top 5 with a separate model. *Metadata.* Store category, date, and source with the chunk, and use them during selection.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: From a product standpoint: **pre-search filtering almost always yields more than improving the search itself.** And the decision on filters is a decision about what the product knows about the request context.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The first version searched across the entire catalog—40 thousand items. Accuracy dropped, and items from other stores that the user does not have access to ended up in the context.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Filtering before search: only items from stores available at the user's address. The corpus shrank from 40 thousand to 3–6 thousand. Quality grew more than from all other improvements combined.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Hybrid search was added because of brands: vector search poorly distinguished between "Domik v derevne" and "Prostokvashino" — to it, these are semantically close dairy brands. The text part solved it.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Reranking: we take 40, return 8. It costs an extra call to a cheap model, about 0.3 kopecks, and noticeably increases the share of correct answers.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The metric we track: the share of queries where the required document made it into the context. Measured on a set of 200 labeled questions. This separates search problems from generation problems.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Improving search has a limit: some questions have no answer in the corpus, and the correct answer is "I don't know". Chasing hundred-percent recall is pointless.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: As the corpus grows, precision drops, and pre-search filtering usually yields more than improving the search itself — and the decision on filters is a product decision.
